title: fitdist
summary: Fit a probability distribution object to sample data.

gpu_support.notes: GPU inputs are gathered to host. Parameter estimation currently runs on CPU.

description: `fitdist(x,distname)` estimates distribution parameters from vector data and returns a `ProbabilityDistribution` object accepted by `pdf`, `cdf`, `icdf`, and `random`.
behaviors: Supported fitted distributions are `"Normal"`, `"Exponential"`, `"Lognormal"`, `"Gamma"`, `"Weibull"`, and `"Poisson"`; common short aliases such as `"norm"`, `"exp"`, `"logn"`, `"gam"`, `"wbl"`, and `"poiss"` are accepted.
Input data must be a numeric vector. `NaN` observations are ignored and `Inf` observations are rejected.
`fitdist(x,distname,"Frequency",w)` accepts nonnegative finite observation weights with one weight per observation. Zero-weight observations are ignored.
Range constraints follow the selected distribution: exponential data must be nonnegative, lognormal/gamma/weibull data must be positive, and Poisson data must be nonnegative integers.

The returned object exposes `DistributionName`, `DistName`, `ParameterNames`, `ParameterValues`, `NumParameters`, `NumObservations`, `NLogL`, `IsTruncated`, and scalar parameter properties such as `mu`, `sigma`, `lambda`, `a`, or `b`.

examples.description: Fit a normal distribution and evaluate it
examples.input: pd = fitdist([1;2;3], "Normal"); y = pdf(pd, 2); p = cdf(pd, 2); x = icdf(pd, 0.5)

faqs.question: Does fitdist support censoring or custom optimization options?
faqs.answer: Not yet. `Censoring`, `Options`, and grouped `By` fits are rejected explicitly rather than ignored.
